Find the total finite area $A$ enclosed between the curves $y=f(x)={x}^{3}-13x-10$ and $y=2,$ as shown above. Do not round the answer.

*(Note: Figure not drawn to scale)*

$A=$

{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Let $g(x)=2.$ First, we find the intersections of the two curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =g(x) \\ {x}^{3}-13x-10 & =2 \\ {x}^{3}-13x-12 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $x=-1$ is a root of ${x}^{3}-13x-12,$ and if we divide ${x}^{3}-13x-12$ by $x+1$ using synthetic division, we get ${x}^{2}-x-12.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+1)({x}^{2}-x-12) & =0 \\ (x+1)(x-4)(x+3) & =0 \\ x & =-3,-1,4.\end{aligned}
$$

The area we want consists of two regions: ${A}_{1}$ and ${A}_{2}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14220560/assets/3c4181d72f44f0190d03fa4239718e4f2877fda19a7b1f87421ef2746e27bcbc.png)

  

- For the area ${A}_{1},$ we have $x\in [-3,-1],$ and the upper function is $f(x)$ while the lower function is $g(x).$ So, the area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & ={\int }_{-3}^{-1}(f(x)-g(x))\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{-1}(({x}^{3}-13x-10)-2)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{-1}({x}^{3}-13x-12)\,\text{d}x \\  & =(\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}-\frac{13}{2}{x}^{2}-12x){|}_{-3}^{-1} \\  & =(\frac{(-1)^{4}}{4}-\frac{13}{2}(-1)^{2}-12(-1))-(\frac{(-3)^{4}}{4}-\frac{13}{2}(-3)^{2}-12(-3)) \\  & =(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{13}{2}+12)-(\frac{81}{4}-\frac{117}{2}+36) \\  & =\frac{23}{4}-(-\frac{9}{4}) \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

- For the area ${A}_{2},$ we have $x\in [-1,4],$ and the upper function is $g(x)$ while the lower function is $f(x).$ So, the area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & ={\int }_{-1}^{4}(g(x)-f(x))\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{4}(2-({x}^{3}-13x-10))\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{\int }_{-1}^{4}({x}^{3}-13x-12)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-(\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}-\frac{13}{2}{x}^{2}-12x){|}_{-1}^{4} \\  & =-(\frac{{4}^{4}}{4}-\frac{13}{2}({4}^{2})-12(4))+(\frac{(-1)^{4}}{4}-\frac{13}{2}(-1)^{2}-12(-1)) \\  & =-(64-104-48)+(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{13}{2}+12) \\  & =-(-88)+(\frac{23}{4}) \\  & =\frac{375}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}=8+\frac{375}{4}=\frac{407}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
